sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: emergency situations: collision avoidance, ABS, skids, drop-offs, vehicle malfunctions and breakdowns
Audience: every first-time South Carolina Class D applicant; these responses matter most to new drivers who have not yet faced an emergency.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the rule to hold firm, constant pressure on an ABS brake pedal rather than pumping it is set out here [A01], and a new permit holder can add emergency contacts to their SCDMV record [A06].
Level: mostly ordered procedures (what to do first, second and third) with one distance value for flares.
Prerequisites: the steering, braking and space-management habits from the earlier sections.

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.
